The idempotency guard and duplicate send detector form a dual pair in autonomous systems. The former ensures that repeated application of an operation yields the same result, while the latter identifies and suppresses redundant operations. These primitives are modeled as functions over event spaces with temporal signatures. In GSI, they enable robust probabilistic inference by filtering out noise from duplicate signals. In GSE, they ensure deterministic behavior in distributed workflows. The failure mode occurs when either guard fails to recognize a true duplicate or allows a false positive, leading to inconsistent states or missed events. The mathematical structure is a categorical duality between event identity and operational stability.
